queer_characters.name: Ignacio / Zahara
queer_characters.notes: Source describes her as a transgender woman; her arc embodies the 'tragic trans death' trope — heroin addiction, sex work, and murder, with her agency repeatedly undermined by exploitative men.
queer_characters.contest_notes: The source labels Ignacio/Zahara a transgender woman, but the character also functions as a drag persona of a boarding-school figure, and such Almodóvar characters are sometimes read as gay men in drag rather than as trans women; the framing is open to interpretation.

queer_characters.name: Enrique Goded
queer_characters.notes: Described as a gay film director and Ignacio's childhood first love; central sympathetic figure, though entangled in the film's manipulation and tragedy.

queer_characters.name: Juan / Angel Andrade
queer_characters.notes: Becomes romantically involved with Berenguer (a man) while impersonating his deceased sibling and concealing involvement in Ignacio's death; a manipulative, deceptive figure. Source states the relationship but does not give a specific label.

queer_characters.name: Father Manolo / Manuel Berenguer
queer_characters.notes: A predatory priest who sexually exploited a child and later becomes romantically involved with Juan; conflates queerness with clerical abuse, a clear predatory-queer portrayal.
